newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oilseed supply seen staying tight through 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Oilseed supply seen staying tight through 1997/98.

text.p: Oilseeds supply will fall short of demand by four million tonnes in 1996/97 and may only exceed demand by one million tonnes in 1997/98, the independent Oil World newsletter said.
It put 1996/97 output of 10 key oilseeds at 257.3 million tonnes, use at 261.3 million and ending stocks at 27.1 million.
It pegged 1997/98 output at 272 million tonnes versus consumption of 271 million, which would give ending stocks of 28.1 million.
The stocks/use ratio in both seasons would be 10.4 percent compared with an average 12.5 percent since 1992.
Output gains would result from higher oilseeds prices, reductions in EU set-aside and releases of land from U.S. conservation programmes, it said.
